statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide a 3D orbit command that rotates the view with the mouse, where horizontal drags move the camera parallel to the WCS XY plane, vertical drags move it along Z, Shift plus mouse wheel enters temporary orbit, and objects cannot be edited meanwhile; documented for the web app only in WebGPU-capable browsers.
notes: Added from help page "3DORBIT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run 3DORBIT and drag horizontally; the view rotates about the target, and holding Shift with the middle button from another command also orbits temporarily.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide ALIGN to move, rotate, scale or tilt objects in 2D and 3D using between one and three pairs of source and destination points, with scaling offered only when two pairs are given.
notes: Added from help page "ALIGN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app select a rectangle, run ALIGN with two source and destination pairs and answer Yes to scale; the rectangle is moved, rotated and scaled so its source points land on the destinations.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must draw an arc through three points (start point, a second point lying on the arc, and endpoint), where each point may be given by object snap or typed distance.
notes: Added from help page "ARC (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run ARC, pick a line endpoint, a second point and an endpoint; a three-point arc through all three points is created.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must create rectangular, path or polar arrays of selected objects or blocks that are associative or non-associative by option, with associative arrays editable through grips, the Properties palette or ARRAYEDIT, including editing sources and replacing or removing items.
notes: Added from help page "ARRAY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a chair, run ARRAY with Rectangular associative and 2 rows by 3 columns; one array object is made, and changing its column count in the Properties palette updates the items.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide ARRAYEDIT to modify an associative rectangular, path or polar array by changing its properties, editing the source objects (propagating to all items), replacing items or source objects, or resetting the base point; this page documents the web app, not desktop AutoCAD.
notes: Added from help page "ARRAYEDIT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a polar array, choose Source, edit one item, and assert every item that shares the source updates; then use Replace on a single item and assert only that item changes.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide an ATTACH command that opens the External References panel; this page documents the web app, not desktop AutoCAD.
notes: Added from help page "ATTACH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run ATTACH and assert the External References panel opens.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide BREAK that splits an object or removes the portion between two points, projecting off-object points onto it and turning a circle into an arc counterclockwise from first to second point; this page documents the web app, not desktop AutoCAD.
notes: Added from help page "BREAK (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, break a line between two points and assert two collinear lines with a gap result; break a circle and assert it becomes an arc.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide BREAKATPOINT to split an open line, arc or open polyline into two objects at one point, projecting an off-object point onto it; this page documents the web app, not desktop AutoCAD.
notes: Added from help page "BREAKATPOINT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run BREAKATPOINT on a line and click a point beside it; assert two segments joined at the projected point.

statement: Provide in the web editor a CHAMFER command, as documented for the AutoCAD web app, that bevels two lines, polyline segments, rays or xlines using Distance or Angle method, with Trim/No Trim, Polyline, Multiple, Undo, and Shift to make a sharp corner.
notes: Added from help page "CHAMFER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, set Distance 2,2 and chamfer two lines meeting at a right angle, and assert both are trimmed and a new line of length 2*sqrt(2) joins their ends.

statement: Provide in the web editor a CIRCLE command, as documented for the AutoCAD web app, that creates a circle from a picked center and a radius picked or typed.
notes: Added from help page "CIRCLE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run CIRCLE, click 0,0 and type radius 5, and assert one circle with center origin and radius 5 exists.

statement: Provide in the web app a CLEANSCREENON command, per the AutoCAD web documentation, that collapses the left side panel of the browsing window, with the panel restored by clicking an icon in the left margin.
notes: Added from help page "CLEANSCREENON (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run CLEANSCREENON and assert the left panel collapses, then click a left-margin icon and assert it re-expands.

statement: Provide in the web editor a COPY command, per the AutoCAD web documentation, that duplicates selected objects from a base point to successive picked points with a preview, ending on Enter, along with clipboard copy and paste shortcuts across drawings.
notes: Added from help page "COPY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a circle, run COPY with a base point and two target points, and assert two copies are created at those offsets.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide a single DIMENSION (DIM) command that previews and creates linear, aligned, angular, radius and diameter dimensions based on the hovered object, with a radius/diameter switch for arcs and circles.
notes: Added from help page "DIMENSION (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run DIM, hover a circle and assert a radius preview, switch to diameter, click to place, and assert a diameter dimension object is created.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must erase selected objects with ERASE (or DELETE), accepting selection options such as Last, Previous and All in place of a manual selection.
notes: Added from help page "ERASE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, draw three lines, run ERASE with the All option, and assert the drawing has no objects.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must break compound objects such as blocks, polylines and regions into their component objects with EXPLODE, noting that color, linetype and lineweight can change.
notes: Added from help page "EXPLODE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, explode a rectangular polyline and assert four separate line objects result.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must extend objects to boundary edges in Quick mode (all objects are boundaries) and Standard mode (select boundaries first), with Fence, Crossing, Project and Edge options and Shift-select to trim.
notes: Added from help page "EXTEND (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run EXTEND in Quick mode on a short line near a boundary and assert it lengthens to the boundary; Shift-select trims instead.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide an EXTERNALREFERENCES command that launches the External References panel.
notes: Added from help page "EXTERNALREFERENCES (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run EXTERNALREFERENCES and assert the External References panel is displayed.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, FILLET must round two 2D objects (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, ellipses, splines, rays, xlines) with a tangent arc of the Radius set, trimming or extending them to meet the arc, leaving circles untrimmed, ignoring segments too short for the radius, and using radius zero to produce a sharp corner.
notes: Added from help page "FILLET (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app set FILLET radius 5, pick two perpendicular lines meeting at a corner and assert a tangent arc of radius 5 is added and both lines are trimmed to its endpoints; repeat with radius 0 and assert the lines simply meet at a point.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, the command-line form -FIND must let the user choose whether the text search covers the entire drawing, only the current space or layout, or only selected objects.
notes: Added from help page "-FIND (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run -FIND in the web app, choose the current layout scope, search for a string present only in model space, and assert no matches are reported.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, FIND must show an editor bar where the user enters a search string (wildcards allowed), picks the search scope (drawing, current space or layout, selection), toggles which object kinds to include (blocks, attributes, xrefs, text, table text, dimension/leader text, hidden items) and match rules, and steps through the hits with next/previous arrows that zoom to each instance and show the hit count.
notes: Added from help page "FIND (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run FIND for 'PUMP' in a drawing with three matching text objects, assert the count shows 3 and pressing next zooms to each in turn.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, FINDINCLUDE must read or set the bit-coded FIND include-objects state (blocks=1, attributes=2, xrefs=4, text=8, table text=16, dimension/leader text=32, hidden items=64) through toggle prompts, with 0 meaning everything off.
notes: Added from help page "FINDINCLUDE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run FINDINCLUDE, enable Blocks and Text only, and assert the underlying value reads 9, and that FIND then skips table text.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, FINDMATCH must read or set the bit-coded FIND matching rules (diacritics=1, wildcards=2, whole words=4, match case=8, half/full width=16), including wildcard syntax such as #, @, ., *, ?, ~, [ ], and escape, with 0 meaning all off.
notes: Added from help page "FINDMATCH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set FINDMATCH to whole words only (value 4), search 'Front Door' and assert the string 'Front Doormat' is not reported.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, GROUP must combine selected objects into a named or unnamed group (with an optional description) so that selecting any member selects all members and the group can be moved, copied, or rotated as a unit, with UNGROUP to dissolve it and objects allowed to belong to several groups.
notes: Added from help page "GROUP (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app select two circles, run GROUP, click one circle and assert both are highlighted; run UNGROUP and assert clicking selects a single circle.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, -HATCH must fill a closed region or chosen objects from the command line using a pattern, solid color, or gradient, supporting internal point picking (with red circles marking boundary gaps), property selection including user-defined patterns and pattern listing, boundary drawing, adding or removing boundaries, and advanced settings.
notes: Added from help page "-HATCH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run -HATCH on a rectangle with one gap, pick inside and assert red gap markers are shown and no hatch is made; close the gap and assert the hatch is created.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, ID must display the X, Y, and Z UCS coordinates of a picked point and store it as the last point so that @ at the next point prompt refers to it.
notes: Added from help page "ID (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run ID, pick (10,20,0), assert the coordinates are reported, then run LINE and enter @5,0 and assert the line starts at (10,20).

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, the program must provide JOIN to merge selected splines, 3D polylines, polylines, elliptical arcs, arcs and lines that share endpoints into a single object, where closed objects cannot be joined.
notes: Added from help page "JOIN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app select two collinear connected lines and run JOIN; they become a single line, and selecting a closed circle is rejected.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, the program must provide LINE to create a chain of contiguous line segments, each a separate object, specified by clicks or dynamic-input distances, with undo of the last segment and Enter to finish.
notes: Added from help page "LINE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run LINE and click three points; two separate line objects result, and undo removes the last segment.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, the program must provide MATCHPROP to copy properties from a source object to selected destination objects, including transparency, plot style, lineweight, linetype scale, linetype, layer and color.
notes: Added from help page "MATCHPROP (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run MATCHPROP, pick a red line on layer A as source and a blue circle as destination; the circle becomes red and moves to layer A.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide a MEASURE command that reports length, angle and radius of objects under the pointer via horizontal and vertical rays, plus Distance, Angle and Area modes driven by picked points.
notes: Added from help page "MEASURE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run MEASURE, choose Distance, pick (0,0) and (3,4), and confirm 5 units with dX 3 and dY 4 are shown; choose Area and pick a unit square and confirm area 1 and perimeter 4.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must mirror selected objects across a line defined by two picked points, creating a mirrored copy.
notes: Added from help page "MIRROR (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a line from (0,0) to (2,1), run MIRROR with axis (0,0)-(0,1), and confirm a copy exists from (0,0) to (-2,1).

statement: The AutoCAD web app must create a multileader with an arrowhead point, landing point and in-place text, and allow editing the text and height of an existing multileader.
notes: Added from help page "MLEADER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run MLEADER, click an arrowhead point, click a landing point, enter 'NOTE', confirm, and verify a multileader with text NOTE exists.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must move selected objects by the displacement between a picked base point and second point.
notes: Added from help page "MOVE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a circle centered at (0,0), run MOVE from (0,0) to (5,5), and confirm the center is now (5,5).

statement: The AutoCAD web app must create and edit multiline text and warn that editing text made in desktop AutoCAD discards its rich formatting, which can be undone.
notes: Added from help page "MTEXT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run MTEXT, pick a corner, type 'Notes', confirm, then double-click it and confirm the text editor opens.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must create a parallel or concentric copy of a selected object at a specified distance on the side the user indicates, working on polylines, circles and arcs.
notes: Added from help page "OFFSET (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run OFFSET with distance 5 on a circle of radius 10 pointing outward, and confirm a circle of radius 15 is created.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, PLINE must create a 2D polyline of connected line and arc segments as one object, switching between line and arc and finishing with Enter or closing back to the first point.
notes: Added from help page "PLINE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app draw a three-segment PLINE with Close and assert one closed polyline with three vertices exists.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, POINT must create a point object at a 2D or 3D location, using the current elevation when Z is omitted, with appearance governed by PDMODE and usable as a snap node.
notes: Added from help page "POINT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run POINT at 5,5 and assert a point exists at 5,5 with the current elevation as Z.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, PROPERTIES must open the Properties panel for viewing and editing selected object properties.
notes: Added from help page "PROPERTIES (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app select a circle, run PROPERTIES and assert the panel shows its radius.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, RECTANGLE must create a rectangular polyline from two opposite corners, with a Dimension option for entering length and width.
notes: Added from help page "RECTANGLE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run RECTANGLE, pick two corners; a closed 4-vertex polyline results, and using Dimension with 10 and 5 gives a 10 by 5 rectangle.

statement: In the AutoCAD web app, REVCLOUD must create rectangular, polygonal or object-based revision clouds and offer an Arc length option setting minimum and maximum arc size, since too small a length makes the cloud look like straight lines.
notes: Added from help page "REVCLOUD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run REVCLOUD, choose Rectangular and pick two corners; a revision cloud of arcs outlines the rectangle, and Object converts a selected circle into a cloud.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide ROTATE to rotate selected objects about a picked base point by a typed angle or by a reference angle aligned to an absolute angle.
notes: Added from help page "ROTATE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a line, run ROTATE with a base point at its start and angle 90, and assert the line endpoint rotated by 90 degrees.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide SCALE that resizes selected objects proportionally using a reference distance specified with two picked points.
notes: Added from help page "SCALE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, select a 10-unit line, run SCALE with a reference length of 10 and a new length of 20, and assert the line is 20 units long.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide SPLINE to create NURBS curves defined either by fit points or by control vertices.
notes: Added from help page "SPLINE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run SPLINE through four fit points and assert a spline object passing through them is created.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide TRIM with Quick mode (all objects act as edges, objects that cannot be trimmed are deleted) and Standard mode (explicit cutting edges), with Fence, Crossing, Project, Edge, Erase and Undo options.
notes: Added from help page "TRIM (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run TRIM in Quick mode, click a line segment between two crossing lines and assert only that segment is removed.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide UCS to set the origin and orientation of the user coordinate system by one, two or three points, along with face alignment and other options, affecting coordinate entry, Ortho and grid.
notes: Added from help page "UCS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app run UCS with origin 10,10 and assert the coordinate 0,0 now maps to world 10,10.

statement: The AutoCAD web app must provide UNGROUP to dissolve a selected group, a group by name, or all groups, with accept/next choices for nested groups.
notes: Added from help page "UNGROUP (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app select a group, run UNGROUP, and assert the group is deleted while its members remain.

statement: The web app documentation requires -VPORTS to create layout viewports by corner points, on, off, fit, lock, object, polygonal, restore and layer override reset, plus splits of 2, 3 and 4, and model space viewport save, restore and join configurations.
notes: Added from help page "-VPORTS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run -VPORTS in a layout, choose Fit, and assert one viewport fills the layout; choose 4 in model space and assert four equal viewports.

statement: The web app documentation requires VSCURRENT to set the current viewport's visual style with the same options as desktop, though the Shaded style is the only one officially supported there.
notes: Added from help page "VSCURRENT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run VSCURRENT and choose Shaded on a 3D solid, and assert the viewport renders the solid with smooth shading.

statement: The web app documentation requires XLINE to create infinite construction lines by two points, horizontal, vertical, angle (absolute or from a reference line), bisector, or offset from an object by distance or through a point.
notes: Added from help page "XLINE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the web app, run XLINE Hor through 0,5 and assert an infinite line parallel to the X axis through y=5 is created.

statement: The AutoCAD web app (as documented for the browser app) must open to a file-manager homepage from which a new drawing is started from a metric or imperial template, and then present a command palette grouped into Draw, Annotate and Modify plus a command line that accepts typed input with command suggestions without first clicking in it.
notes: Added from help page "Basics"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Sign in, click New Drawing, pick Metric and open it; type 'CIR' with no click in the command line and verify the typed text appears there with suggestion entries listed.

statement: The web app must offer a reduced set of 2D drawing tools (line, polyline, circle, rectangle and similar) that are started from the palette or by typed command or alias, with points picked in the drawing area or given as a length through dynamic input.
notes: Added from help page "Geometry"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Type L, Enter, click a first point, move the cursor right, type 100 and Enter in the dynamic input field and verify a horizontal line of length 100 is created.

statement: The web app must provide dynamic input, object snaps and polar tracking as its principal precision aids, with polar tracking enabled by default and restricting the cursor to horizontal and vertical directions while a distance is being typed.
notes: Added from help page "Precision"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Start LINE, click a point, move right and type 50: verify a horizontal 50-unit segment; then hover near an existing line's endpoint and verify an endpoint snap marker appears.

statement: The web app must let users organize objects on layers through a Layers panel in which a layer can be made current, switched off or on with a light-bulb toggle, locked, and given properties, with new objects landing on the current layer.
notes: Added from help page "Layers"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open the Layers panel, switch off the layer holding doors, and verify those doors disappear while other layers remain visible; draw a line and verify it is on the current layer.

statement: The web app must offer a Properties panel that shows and edits color, linetype and other properties of the selected objects, shows the current layer's properties when nothing is selected, and resolves ByLayer values from the layer.
notes: Added from help page "Properties"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a ByLayer wall line, change its color to red in the Properties panel and verify the line turns red and reports a non-ByLayer color; deselect and verify the panel shows the current layer's properties.

statement: The web app must support annotation with multiline text (MTEXT, in-place editor with height in drawing units, resizable box by grips, double-click to edit) and multileaders (MLEADER) that can be modified after creation, as well as dimensioning.
notes: Added from help page "Annotate and Dimension"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run MT, pick two corners, type a note at height 100 and exit; verify the text height is 100 units and double-clicking reopens the editor; run MLD and verify a leader with text is created.

statement: The web app must allow switching from model space to paper-space layouts that contain layout viewports displaying model space at a chosen scale, where a viewport can be selected, copied, resized with grips and entered by double-click to pan and zoom, before output to PDF.
notes: Added from help page "Layout and Print"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Switch to Layout1, select the viewport and set a 1:50 scale, copy it with COPY, double-click inside the copy to pan, double-click outside to exit, and verify the first viewport's view is unchanged.

statement: The web app's homepage must act as a file manager that can upload, delete, rename, move and download files, create folders and new drawings from metric, imperial or custom templates, show Files versus Shared with me per storage source, and list items created in the mobile app or saved to the web from desktop.

source.ref: About the Homepage and File Manager

notes: Added from help page "About the Homepage and File Manager"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Upload a DWG to a folder, rename it, move it into a new folder, and verify the shared-column icon appears for a drawing owned by someone else under Shared with me.

statement: The web app must support selecting objects by click, window (left to right, fully enclosed) and crossing (right to left, touching) boxes, Shift-removal from the selection set, and basic editing commands such as ERASE, MOVE and TRIM from the Modify group.
notes: Added from help page "Modify"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Drag a box right-to-left across three lines of which one is only partly inside and verify all three are selected; Shift-click one and verify two remain; run E and verify they are deleted.

statement: The web app must show an Activity Insights palette for drawings saved to Forma Data Management that records and displays contributors' activities such as new drawing, saved versions, saved-to-other-format, xref references and purge or audit, including activities from other AutoCAD products even when the web app cannot perform them.
notes: Added from help page "Activity Insights"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save two versions of a Forma-hosted drawing, purge it in desktop, then open it on the web and verify tiles for both versions and for the purge appear with the contributor names.

statement: The web app must connect to Autodesk Drive, Forma Data Management, Box, Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive by means of sign-in and permission grant so that drawings stored there can be viewed, edited and saved, support several accounts for each provider, and allow a provider to be disconnected.
notes: Added from help page "Cloud Storage Providers"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Add a Google Drive storage provider, open a drawing from it, edit and save; add a second Google account and verify both appear; disconnect one and verify its files vanish from the list.

statement: The web app's AutoLISP support must accommodate dialog definitions stored in DCL (dialog control language) text files, loaded for use by LISP routines, and follow the layout guidelines of uncluttered, logically grouped and aligned tiles with tab order following natural data entry order.
notes: Added from help page "About Designing Dialog Boxes (DCL)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a DCL file defining a dialog with X, Y and Z edit boxes from a LISP routine and verify the dialog displays them aligned in X, Y, Z tab order.

statement: The web app must let a user connect Forma Data Management accounts as a storage provider by choosing projects to connect, after which drawings in those projects are viewable, editable and savable subject to the project owner's permissions.
notes: Added from help page "Connect to Forma Data Management"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Add storage provider, pick Forma Data Management, select one project and verify its files are listed in the file manager and that a user lacking edit permission cannot save.

statement: The web app must allow connecting a local folder as a storage provider by browsing to it and granting the site read-write access each session, making all files in that folder available in the file manager, in Chromium-based browsers only.
notes: Added from help page "Connect to Locally Stored Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Choose Local Files, browse to a folder, grant access, verify the folder's drawings are listed; reload in a new session and verify access must be granted again.

statement: The web app and other products must be able to resolve drawing dependencies (templates, sheet-set templates, fonts, hatch patterns, linetypes, plot style tables, LISP and DCL files) from support-file folders shared by a Forma Data Management project, configured only by project administrators, so every member automatically uses the project's approved files.
notes: Added from help page "Connected Support Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set up a project's support folder containing a custom font, open a project drawing as a different member without local configuration, and verify the font resolves from the project.

statement: The web app must offer a project-administrator-only wizard on a connected Forma Data Management project (Project Support Files, Set Up Project, Begin Setup) that creates a hidden support folder and uses it as the starting point for searching support files.

source.ref: Set Up Connected Support Files for a Forma Project

notes: Added from help page "To Set Up a Forma Data Management Project to Use Connected Support Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: As a project administrator run the setup wizard and verify a '.autodesk.support' folder is created in the project; verify a non-administrator cannot see the setup option.

statement: The web app must provide COMPARE for drawings stored in Forma Data Management, diffing the latest saved state of the open drawing against another file or an earlier version chosen in Activity Insights, marking differences with colors and revision clouds while editing tools stay disabled and only View, Measure and Find remain available.
notes: Added from help page "Drawing Compare"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run COMPARE, pick another drawing, verify differences are shown in color with revision clouds and that MOVE is unavailable while in compare mode; with unsaved changes verify a save-or-discard prompt.

statement: The web app must let a project administrator edit an ordered list of Forma Data Management folders as the support-file search paths of a project, where earlier entries win when the same file occurs in several folders.
notes: Added from help page "To Set the Paths for Connected Support Files of a Forma Data Management Project"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Add two folders each holding a different 'x.pat', order them, verify the first folder's file is used; reorder and verify the other is used.

statement: The web app must offer sharing of a drawing link with options depending on storage: markup, edit or view-only for Forma Data Management drawings, copy or view-only for non-Forma drawings, and provider-controlled permissions for drawings in third-party cloud storage.
notes: Added from help page "Share"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a Forma-hosted drawing and verify the Share dialog lists Markup, Can Edit and View Only; open a local drawing and verify only copy and view-only appear.

statement: The web app must treat Connected Support Files as project-aware support files shared among every member of a project in Forma Data Management, across desktop and web, available only for drawings stored in an organized project and configurable by project administrators.
notes: Added from help page "FAQs: Working with Connected Support Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Configure connected support files from desktop, open a project drawing in the web app and verify the same support files are found.

statement: The web app must be able to share a Forma Data Management drawing in Markup mode, creating one trace per Model or layout tab with a stable URL, so project members can add and publish markups without modifying the drawing itself.
notes: Added from help page "Sharing an Autodesk Forma Data Management Drawing for Multi-user Markup"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click SHARE, choose Markup, Copy Link; share again from the same tab and verify the identical URL; open it as a collaborator, add a markup, and verify the DWG is unchanged.

statement: The web app must display drawings without altering their data while omitting unsupported content (proxy and vertical-product custom objects, point clouds, underlays, some images and xrefs) and substituting fonts with Simplex, allow uploading missing xrefs, and display only JPG, PNG, GIF and BMP images.
notes: Added from help page "Objects Missing in Drawing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a DWG containing a PDF underlay and an unsupported custom object: verify they are not shown and the file is unchanged on save; upload a missing xref via XREF and verify it appears.

statement: The web app must support sharing a Forma-hosted drawing using the Can Edit permission through a copied link so that recipients with sufficient project permissions can modify the drawing itself.
notes: Added from help page "Share an Autodesk Forma Data Management drawing for Editing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open the Share dialog on a Forma drawing, select Can Edit, copy the link, open it as a project member with edit rights and verify edits save to the original drawing.

statement: The web app must open drawings and folders shared from Box, Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive with the provider's permissions, treating drawings shared without edit rights as view-only where layers and object properties can be inspected but nothing modified.

source.ref: Share Drawings from a Cloud Storage Provider (web)

notes: Added from help page "Share Drawings from a Cloud Storage Provider"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing shared view-only from Dropbox, verify the layers and Properties can be read, and that a MOVE attempt is blocked.

statement: The web app must create a share link to a transmittal-style copy of the current drawing including xrefs, images and fonts, expiring after seven days, with View only or Edit and save a copy permissions that never alter the sharer's original file.
notes: Added from help page "Share Drawing (Share URL)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Share a drawing with an xref as 'Edit and save a copy', open the link, edit and save, and verify the sender's original is unchanged and the xref is saved beside the copy; verify the link fails after seven days.

statement: The web app must load and run basic AutoLISP routines from a LISP tab with a Manage LISP support-files uploader, a per-drawing namespace so symbols do not conflict between open drawings, and an option to choose routines that run at the start of every drawing open, while unsupported functions fail.
notes: Added from help page "LISP files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Upload a routine setting (setq a (getvar "DWGNAME")), load it in two open drawings and verify 'a' holds each drawing's own name; mark a routine for startup and verify it runs on next open.

statement: The web app must allow uploading custom drawing templates through New Drawing and the Drawing Templates list so they can be chosen for new drawings.
notes: Added from help page "Upload Drawing Templates"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Choose New Drawing, Add Drawing Templates, upload a DWT and verify it appears in the template drop-down and a new drawing created from it carries its settings.

statement: The web app must clearly reject or not open the formats it does not support, such as 3DS, SAT, Inventor, CATIA, DGN, DXF, FBX, IGES, JT, Parasolid, PDF, Pro/ENGINEER, Rhino, SolidWorks, WMF and STEP files, while still opening DWG.
notes: Added from help page "Unsupported File Formats"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Try uploading a STEP and a DXF file and verify they are reported as unsupported; open a DWG and verify success.

statement: The web app must provide an Open in Desktop action that saves the drawing in the 2018 file format and launches it in an installed desktop AutoCAD (2018 or later) through an installable plug-in on Windows or macOS.
notes: Added from help page "Open in Desktop"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click Open in Desktop with the plug-in installed and verify the drawing is saved and opens in desktop AutoCAD; without the plug-in verify a download prompt is shown.

statement: The web app must allow uploading custom hatch pattern files from the support-files manager or from the Pattern Name list of a selected hatch's Properties palette.
notes: Added from help page "Upload Hatch Patterns"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a hatch, open Pattern Name, Add Hatch Patterns, upload a PAT file and verify the new pattern can be applied to the hatch.

statement: The web app must allow uploading font files in the support-files manager so drawings can use them.
notes: Added from help page "Upload Fonts"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In Manage Support Files choose Fonts, upload a TTF, open a drawing using that font and verify the text renders in it instead of the substitute.

statement: The web app must allow uploading CTB or STB plot style tables from the support-files manager or from the Plot style list of the model Properties palette.
notes: Added from help page "Upload Plot Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: From Model Properties click Plot style, Add Plot Styles, upload a CTB and verify it is selectable and used when plotting to PDF.

statement: The web app must expose the Forma Data Management Issues tool for drawings shared in Markup mode, giving collaborators an issue list, a Markup palette and an Issue form for creating, review and add information to issues.
notes: Added from help page "Issues for Web"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Share a Forma drawing in Markup mode, open it as a collaborator, create an issue in the form and verify it appears in the issues list for others.

statement: The web app's Layers panel must toggle layer visibility with a light bulb, change a layer color from drawing colors or the AutoCAD color index, create a new layer, and lock a layer.
notes: Added from help page "Layers"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click the bulb for layer A and verify its objects hide; click the lock and verify its objects cannot be edited; choose color 1 and verify the layer's ByLayer objects turn red.

statement: The web app's command line docked at lower left must accept typed commands with suggestions that can be chosen by click or arrow keys, and show prompts whose options (such as 3P in CIRCLE) can be chosen by click or typing.
notes: Added from help page "Command Line"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Type 'CI' and verify suggestions include CIRCLE; run CIRCLE, then click the 3P option in the prompt and verify the 3-point prompt appears.

statement: The web app's Blocks palette must use an assistant to sort blocks into meaningful categories adjustable by conversation and to search blocks by the kind of object they depict rather than by name only (technology preview).
notes: Added from help page "Block Auto-Categorization and Search"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With blocks named B1 and B2 whose shapes are doors, click Categorize blocks with AI and verify a doors category exists; search 'door' and verify those blocks are listed.

statement: The web app must offer dynamic input near the cursor for entering values such as distance, length and angle during commands, and right-click shortcut menus giving repeat last command, cancel and the current command's options.
notes: Added from help page "Dynamic Input and Shortcut Menus"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Start LINE, enter a length via dynamic input and verify the length; right-click mid-command and verify menu entries for Cancel and the command's options.

statement: The web app must generate an editable block from a plain-language description through the Autodesk Assistant from the Blocks tab (AI Block), allow iterative refinement, insert the result into the drawing and Blocks palette, and not retain it if not inserted (technology preview).
notes: Added from help page "Block Generate with AI"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click AI Block, request 'round table with four chairs', click Insert in drawing and verify an editable block reference appears in the Blocks palette that can be moved and scaled.

statement: The web app must export the drawing to PDF through PLOT choosing model-space current display (scaled to fit) or current/all layouts (1:1 per layout paper size), with plot style (acad, Grayscale, monochrome, None), paper size and orientation, delivering a notification link, with optional save to Docs.
notes: Added from help page "Plot to PDF"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run PLOT in model space with Landscape and Grayscale and verify a PDF is produced scaled to fit with a notification link; run it on a layout and verify the PDF is 1:1 on the layout paper size.

statement: The web app's Properties tab must show and change layer, color, linetype, linetype scale, dimension style, text style and multileader style of objects, using styles and linetypes already in the drawing without creating new ones.
notes: Added from help page "Object Properties"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a text object, switch its text style to another existing one in the Properties tab and verify it changes; verify no option to create a new linetype is offered.

statement: The web app's BLOCK command must open a Blocks panel with Current drawing, Recent and Libraries tabs, Create block (via -BLOCK), Browse for blocks, library of up to ten recent paths, and block properties showing selected block name and reference count; inserting a drawing file imports its block definitions.
notes: Added from help page "Blocks Panel"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run BLOCK, verify the three tabs, select a block placed four times and verify the count shows 4; insert a drawing file and verify its block definitions are added.

statement: The web app must edit objects with grips: select an object, click a grip and move to stretch it, with grips on text, blocks, line midpoints, circle centers and points moving instead, Shift for multiple grips preserving the shape between them, and no grips on locked layers.
notes: Added from help page "Grips"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a line, move its endpoint grip and verify it stretches; move its midpoint grip and verify the whole line moves; lock its layer and verify no grips appear.

statement: The web app must support object snaps at any point prompt, including endpoint, midpoint, center, geometric center, node, quadrant, intersection, extension, insertion, perpendicular and others, with apparent intersection interaction noted.
notes: Added from help page "Object Snaps"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a circle and a line, start LINE, hover over the circle's center and verify the center marker, then midpoint of the other line, and verify a line is created between those points.

statement: The web app must offer Publish from the file manager to export a drawing's model space and sheets, or only sheets, as one multi-page PDF or separate PDFs per sheet taking plot style, paper size and orientation from each sheet, continuing even if the browser tab is closed.
notes: Added from help page "Batch Publish to PDF"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Right-click a drawing, Publish, choose sheets only and separate PDFs and verify one PDF per sheet is saved to the chosen location.

statement: The web app must pan and zoom using mouse wheel button drag, wheel roll and trackpad gestures (with Ctrl or Command modifiers), a reversible zoom direction, Zoom Extents via button or middle-button double-click, and Zoom Window.
notes: Added from help page "Pan and Zoom"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Roll the wheel forward and verify zoom in; double-click the middle button and verify the view fits all objects; choose Zoom Window, pick two corners and verify the view fits that window.

statement: The web app must allow selecting before or during commands by clicking, window selection (left to right) or crossing selection (right to left), with Shift adding or removing objects from the selection set.
notes: Added from help page "Select Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select two circles by window left-to-right, Shift-click one to remove it, run ERASE and verify only the remaining one is deleted.

statement: The web app must provide polar tracking restricting cursor movement to specified angles, with on/off and increment angle configurable in Settings.
notes: Added from help page "Polar Tracking"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set the polar increment to 45, start LINE, move the cursor near 45 degrees and verify it is constrained to that angle.

statement: The web app's status bar, at its bottom right, must toggle ortho, polar tracking, object snaps and object snap tracking and open the running settings for them.
notes: Added from help page "Status bar"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click the ortho toggle and verify LINE is constrained to horizontal or vertical; open the running object snap settings and verify the entries are listed.

statement: The web app must expose block libraries (a drawing or folder path set in desktop) and recent blocks across web and desktop through a supported cloud storage provider, plus favorite blocks.

source.ref: Block Libraries, Recent Blocks, Favorite Blocks (web)

notes: Added from help page "Block Libraries, Recent Blocks, and Favorite Blocks"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set a library folder in desktop on Dropbox, open the web Blocks palette and verify the same library blocks and recently inserted blocks appear.

statement: The web app must offer a Views list to switch to Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front, Back and the four isometric orientations as well as named views created in desktop.
notes: Added from help page "Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Choose SE Isometric and verify the view changes to that orientation; verify a named view saved in desktop is listed.

statement: The web app must support blocks as single compound objects with a definition (name, base point, objects) whose changes propagate to all references, references, attributes carrying data, and creation of a block definition through -BLOCK with name, base point and selection.
notes: Added from help page "Blocks"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a block via -BLOCK, insert it twice, edit the definition and verify both references update.

statement: The web app must let the user set the drawing's linear format (scientific, decimal, engineering, architectural, fractional) and angular format (decimal degrees, deg/min/sec, gradians, radians, surveyor's units) with precision for each, where precision affects displayed values of created objects but not dimension precision, which comes from the dimension style.
notes: Added from help page "Units"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set linear format to Architectural with precision 1/16 and angular format to Deg/Min/Sec, then query a 10.5-unit line and its angle and assert they display in those formats while an existing dimension keeps its dimension-style precision.

statement: The web app must provide a Styles Library where named text styles (font, line spacing, justification, color) can be created and modified, with all text objects using a style updating when it changes, per-object overrides allowed, styles governing notes, leaders, dimensions, tables and block attribute text, and an undeletable STANDARD style.
notes: Added from help page "About Text Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create style 'Notes' with a different font, apply it to two texts, change its font and assert both texts update; attempt to delete STANDARD and assert it is refused.

statement: The web app must save the current drawing from a Save button or the Ctrl/Cmd+S shortcut, offer Save As via a drop-down or the SAVE and SAVEAS commands for new name or location, and write the file in the AutoCAD 2018 format regardless of the original version.
notes: Added from help page "Save a Drawing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a 2013-format DWG in the web app, edit, press Ctrl+S, and assert the saved file reports the 2018 format; use Save As with a new name and assert a second file exists.

statement: The web app must let users create new layouts from the views tab with paper size, plot style (acad, grayscale, monochrome, none) and orientation properties, and create and edit paper-space viewports whose scale is chosen from a list, which can be moved or resized by grips, copied to add more, and given a Display Locked property, while layouts with unsupported paper sizes have read-only properties.
notes: Added from help page "Layouts and Layout Viewports"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click + New Layout, set A3 landscape, copy the viewport, set one to 1:50 and lock its display, then assert zoom inside the locked viewport does not change its scale and the copy exists.

statement: The web app must provide an Xrefs side panel to attach DWG and image (JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP) references at a chosen insertion point, resolve missing paths (same-folder lookup or explicit path), and detach, unload or reload references from a context menu.
notes: Added from help page "External References"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach a DWG xref, unload it and assert its geometry disappears, reload it and assert it returns, then detach and assert it leaves the Xrefs list.

statement: The web app must supply a standard linetype library and allow users to upload their own custom linetype files through the Linetype drop-down's Add Linetypes option in the Properties panel.
notes: Added from help page "About Custom Linetypes and Linetype Definitions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Upload a custom linetype file via Add Linetypes, assert the new linetype appears in the Linetype drop-down, assign it to a line and assert it renders with that pattern.

statement: The web app must offer a header Settings menu, usable while a command is active, for polar tracking on/off and angle increment, object snaps on/off, drawing units, and navigation that inverts the mouse-wheel zoom sense (standard or reverse).
notes: Added from help page "Settings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With LINE active, open Settings, set polar increment to 15 and zoom direction to Reverse, then assert polar tracking snaps at 15 degrees and wheel-back zooms in.

statement: The web app must be available in a defined set of interface languages and let the user choose between English and the browser's default language in Settings, applying the change after a refresh.
notes: Added from help page "Languages"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set browser language to German, choose German in Settings, refresh and assert the UI is German; choose English, refresh and assert it reverts.

statement: The web app must expose a restricted command-line set of drafting, modify, annotation, layer, block, view, plot-to-PDF, xref, trace and sharing commands (and the PDMODE-style variables) that can be launched by typing, even though not every desktop command or variable is available.
notes: Added from help page "Commands and System Variables"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Type each listed command name (for example LINE, TRIM, REVCLOUD, VSCURRENT) at the command line and assert it launches, and assert an unlisted desktop command is reported unknown.

statement: The web app must provide UNDO and REDO via buttons, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Y, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z) and the command line, where UNDO accepts a count to reverse several operations at once.
notes: Added from help page "UNDO and REDO (Commands)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw four lines, type UNDO 3 and assert one line remains, then press Ctrl+Y and assert one line is restored.

statement: The web app must support Trace, an overlay layer on a drawing where collaborators add markups and design details without altering the original drawing, creatable in desktop, web and mobile, saved with the drawing and surfaced to recipients as notifications.
notes: Added from help page "About Trace"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a trace, draw a line in it, save and reopen the drawing, and assert the line is stored in the trace while the model-space entity count is unchanged.

statement: The product line must provide cross-platform collaboration features across desktop, web and mobile, namely Trace and Checkout, so that work started in one app is usable in the others.
notes: Added from help page "About Cross Platform Features"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a trace on the web client, open the same drawing in the desktop client and assert the trace is listed and viewable.

statement: The web app must let users create traces from the Traces palette, toggle between editing the trace and the drawing (TRACEEDIT/TRACEVIEW), block SAVE variants while a trace is open, edit only their own contributions, copy trace objects into the drawing with COPYFROMTRACE, and rename, delete or remove contributions from their own traces, with TRACEOSNAP controlling snapping to trace geometry.
notes: Added from help page "Working With Trace"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a trace, draw a circle, run COPYFROMTRACE on it and assert the drawing gains a circle at the same place while the trace keeps its copy; assert QSAVE is refused while the trace is open.

statement: The product must import marked-up PDF, JPG or PNG files as an overlay in the Trace environment, automatically classify markups (text, clouds, strikethroughs, instruction words such as move or rotate) using cloud-based recognition, and let Markup Assist convert them into drawing text, clouds or revisions to existing geometry.

source.ref: About Markup Import and Markup Assist (web app)

notes: Added from help page "About Markup Import and Markup Assist"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Import a PDF containing a hand-drawn circle and handwritten note, assert both are detected as markups, and insert the circle as a revision cloud via Markup Assist.

statement: The web app must provide an Open in Desktop action that saves the current drawing and opens it in a locally installed desktop product of version 2018 or newer through an installable companion plug-in.
notes: Added from help page "Open in Desktop"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Click Open in Desktop with the plug-in installed and assert the drawing is saved and then opened in the desktop application; with it missing assert a download prompt appears.

statement: The Trace environment must provide settings sliders for overlay opacity (TRACEPAPERCTL), fading of geometry (TRACEFADECTL, governed by TRACEFRONT/TRACEBACK), imported-markup background transparency (MARKUPPAPERTRANSPARENCY) and faded markup transparency (TRACEMARKUPFADECTL).
notes: Added from help page "Trace Settings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a trace, move the Overlay Effect slider and assert TRACEPAPERCTL changes to the corresponding value and the tracing-paper overlay opacity changes.

statement: The product must support Checkout, where a collaborator with a read-only copy of a cloud-managed drawing checks out selected objects into a trace (locking them for the editor), edits them, submits and closes it, and the read-write editor is notified and can review and merge or cancel, with a backup trace kept, while web and mobile can only view checkouts.
notes: Added from help page "About Checkout"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing read-only, run CHECKOUT on a rectangle, move it in the trace, submit and close, then as the editor merge and assert the rectangle moved and a backup trace exists.

statement: The product must create a link (SHARE) to a cloud-managed drawing, rather than a copy, with three permission levels (markup, view-only, editable), that project members open in the web or mobile app and that always points to the latest saved version.

source.ref: Share a link to a cloud-managed drawing (web app)

notes: Added from help page "Share a link (URL) to a Forma Data Management drawing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Share a link with View Only, open it as another project member and assert the drawing displays but cannot be edited; with Can Edit assert an edit changes the original file.

statement: The product must let users import a markup file (PDF or raster image) into a trace, auto-align it or manually align it by source/destination points, and use Markup Assist (under TRACEBACK and MARKUPASSISTMODE) to insert identified text as MTEXT or MLEADER, update existing text, insert revision clouds, fade handled markups or copy text to the clipboard.

source.ref: Working With Markup Import and Markup Assist (web app)

notes: Added from help page "Working With Markup Import and Markup Assist"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Import a scanned markup, align it with two point pairs, click a detected text markup, choose Insert as Mtext and assert an MTEXT with that text is created and the markup fades.

statement: The product must provide a Share Drawing action on the Collaborate tab that generates a link to view or edit the drawing in the web or mobile app, including its related xrefs and images, with view-only, edit, or (for cloud-managed drawings) markup permissions.

source.ref: Share a link to a drawing (web app)

notes: Added from help page "To Share a link (URL) to a drawing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Share a drawing that has an xref as view only, open the link in the web app and assert both the drawing and the xref display.

statement: The product must import published markups from a cloud-managed PDF into the Trace environment and keep them synchronized, so updates to the PDF markups are visible in the drawing, with revisions viewable by collaborators.

source.ref: Forma Data Management Markup Import (web app)

notes: Added from help page "About Forma Data Management Markup Import"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Link a cloud PDF with markups to a drawing, add a new markup to the PDF, refresh and assert the new markup appears in the trace.

statement: The SHARE command must create a link to a duplicate of the active drawing, packaged like ETRANSMIT with xrefs and fonts, that opens in the web or mobile app, expires after seven days, and has View only or Edit and save a copy permission.
notes: Added from help page "Share Drawing (Share URL)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Share with View only, open the link in a browser and assert saving or downloading is blocked; share with Edit and save a copy and assert the recipient can save a copy with xrefs, and that the link fails after seven days.

statement: The product must let a user share the current model or layout of a cloud-managed drawing for markup, creating a new trace and saving the drawing so that project collaborators can add construction-cloud markups to it without modifying the drawing geometry.
notes: Added from help page "Sharing a Forma Data Management Drawing for Multi-user Markup"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Choose Share > Markup, copy the link, open it as a collaborator, add a markup and assert it is stored in the trace and attempts to edit drawing geometry are refused.
